question.explanation:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying both sides by $2{:}$ \begin{align*} \require{cancel} \dfrac{7-3x}{2} &\gt 2 \\[5pt] 2\cdot \left(\dfrac {7-3x} {2}\right) &\gt 2\cdot 2 \\[5pt] \cancel{2}\cdot \left(\dfrac {7-3x} {\cancel{2}}\right) &\gt 2\cdot 2 \\[5pt] 7-3x &\gt 4 \end{align*}

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles.

Remember, when we divide an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

\begin{align*} 7-3x &\gt 4 \\[5pt] 7 - 3x - 7 &\gt 4 - 7 \\[5pt] -3x &\gt {-3} \\[5pt] \dfrac{-3x}{-3} &\,\,{\color{red}{\lt}}\,\, \dfrac{-3}{-3} \\[5pt] x &\lt 1 \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution is $x < 1.$

example.title: Solving Inequalities by Clearing a Rational Expression

question.explanation:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying both sides by $4{:}$

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} 3a -7 &> \dfrac {8a +5} {4} \\[5pt] 4\cdot(3a -7) &> 4 \cdot \left(\dfrac{8a +5}{4}\right) \\[5pt] 4\cdot(3a -7) &> \cancel{4} \cdot \left(\dfrac{8a +5}{\cancel{4}}\right) \\[5pt] 4\cdot(3a -7) &> 8a+5 \\[5pt] 12a-28 &> 8a+5 \end{align*}

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles:

\[ \eqalign{ 12a-28 &> 8a+5 \\[5pt] 12a-28-8a &> 8a+5-8a \\[5pt] 4a-28 &> {5} \\[5pt] 4a-28 +28 &> {5} +28 \\[5pt] 4a &> {33} \\[5pt] \dfrac{4a}{4} &> \dfrac{33}{4} \\[5pt] a &> \dfrac{33}{4} } \]

Therefore, the solution is $a > \dfrac{33}{4}.$

example.title: Inequalities With Rational Expression and Variables on Both Sides

question.explanation:
First, we clear the rational expressions by multiplying both sides of the inequality by the lowest common positive multiple of the denominators:

\begin{align*} \dfrac{3z+1}{2} &> \dfrac{-28+6z}{7} \\[5pt] 14\cdot\left(\dfrac{3z+1}{2}\right) &> 14\cdot\left(\dfrac{-28+6z}{7}\right) \\[5pt] 7\cdot (3z+1) &> 2 \cdot (-28+6z) \\[5pt] 21z+ 7 &> -56+12z \end{align*}

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles:

\begin{align*} 21z + 7 &> -56 +12z \\[5pt] 21z + 7 -12z &> -56 +12z -12z \\[5pt] 9z + 7 &> -56 \\[5pt] 9z + 7 - 7 &> -56 - 7 \\[5pt] 9z &> {-63} \\[5pt] \dfrac{9z}{9} &> \dfrac{-63}{9} \\[5pt] z &> -7 \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution is $z > -7.$

example.title: Solving Inequalities by Clearing Two Rational Expressions

question.text: Find the solution to the inequality $\dfrac{3 - 5z}{8} \leq 6 - 2z.$
question.explanation:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying both sides by $8{:}$ \begin{align*} \require{cancel} \dfrac{3 - 5z}{8} & \leq 6 - 2z\\[5pt] 8 \cdot \left( \dfrac{3 - 5z}{8} \right) & \leq 8 \cdot (6 - 2z) \\[5pt] \cancel{8} \cdot \left( \dfrac{3 - 5z}{\cancel{8}} \right) & \leq 8 \cdot (6 - 2z) \\[5pt] 3 - 5z & \leq 48 - 16z \end{align*}

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles:

\begin{align*} 3 - 5z & \leq 48 - 16z \\[5pt] 3 - 5z + 16z & \leq 48 - 16z + 16z\\[5pt] 3 + 11z & \leq 48\\[5pt] 3 + 11z - 3 & \leq 48 - 3\\[5pt] 11z & \leq 45 \\[5pt] \dfrac{11z}{11} & \leq \dfrac{45}{11} \\[5pt] z & \leq \dfrac{45}{11} \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution is $z \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\leq} \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{45}{11}}.$

example.title: Inequalities With Rational Expression and Variables on Both Sides

question.text: Find the solution to the inequality $\dfrac{x + 6}{4} \gt \dfrac{2x}{3}.$
question.explanation:
First, we clear the rational expressions by multiplying both sides of the inequality by the lowest common positive multiple of the denominators: \begin{align*} \dfrac{x + 6}{4} & \gt \dfrac{2x}{3}\\[5pt] 12\cdot\left(\dfrac{x + 6}{4}\right) & \gt 12\cdot\left(\dfrac{2x}{3}\right)\\[5pt] 3 \cdot (x + 6) & \gt 4 \cdot 2x \\[5pt] 3x + 18 & \gt 8x \end{align*}

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles.

Remember, when we divide an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

\begin{align*} 3x + 18 & \gt 8x\\[5pt] 3x + 18 - 8x & \gt 8x - 8x\\[5pt] 18 - 5x & \gt 0\\[5pt] 18 - 5x - 18 & \gt 0-18\\[5pt] - 5x & \gt -18\\[5pt] \dfrac{- 5x}{-5} & \,\,{\color{red}\lt}\,\, \dfrac{-18}{-5}\\[5pt] x & \lt \dfrac{18}{5} \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution is $x \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\lt} \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{18}{5}}.$
